# Legendary Retreats — Be Legendary

> Be Legendary designs and leads immersive, fully custom executive leadership retreats for CEOs and their senior leadership teams. Every retreat is engineered around one outcome the client defines, then reinforced for 30 days afterward so the behavioral change is measurable — not momentary. Founded and led by James Carter, with 25 years inside executive teams.

## What makes Legendary Retreats different
- **Function before format.** We begin with two questions — "What do you want your people walking away feeling, thinking, and saying to one another?" and "If you could achieve only one thing on this retreat, what would it be?" The answer defines the *function*; every element of the retreat is then engineered to serve it.
- **Format follows function.** The environment, activities, and conversations are chosen for the outcome, never for how they photograph. Formats are interchangeable tools: off-road immersion, open-water sailing, jungle trek, remote lodge ("cabin fever"), five-star estate, horseback/ranch, high-alpine expedition — and, when it serves the outcome, deliberately rough settings like an 1800s mining lodge.
- **30-day reinforcement.** Daily behavioral prompts, tracking, and facilitator re-engagement after the retreat, closing with a behavioral-change report measured against a baseline. One $3B enterprise leadership team posted a 209% mindset-score gain measured 30 days post-retreat.
- **Led by James Carter.** 25 years inside executive teams; hundreds of executive leadership-team retreats designed and led. Co-author alongside Stephen Covey, Ken Blanchard, Deepak Chopra, and Brian Tracy. Featured by CNN, CNN Money, and Business Insider.
- **Social enterprise.** Every executive who attends sends a young person aged 12–15 into a leadership workshop of their own — Be Legendary and the attending executive help the next generation step up and lead.

## Who it's for
CEOs and senior leadership teams of roughly 5–12, most often at companies scaling through real complexity where executive misalignment carries a measurable cost.

## Where
Most retreats run across the United States (40 of 50 states to date), with select retreats in Central America and worldwide on request. Example U.S. destinations: Moab UT, the San Juan Mountains CO, the Sierra Nevada and Great Basin Desert, Sedona AZ, Montana & the Rockies, Death Valley CA.

## Investment
Most multi-day executive retreats for a team of 8–12 run $75,000–$500,000, fully turnkey (facilitation, lodging, meals, activities, transfers, and the 30-day reinforcement system).

Each destination page is written for both "executive retreat in [place]" and "executive offsite in [place]" intent.
- [Field Notes](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/field-notes): Essays by James Carter. Key pieces: "Do leadership retreats actually work?"; "The two questions that define a great leadership retreat" (function before format); "How to align a leadership team pulling in different directions"; "12 questions to ask before any executive retreat" (planning checklist); "What a 30-day reinforcement actually looks like"; "What is an experiential leadership retreat?" (format follows function, retreats are workouts, growth happens in recovery); "How much does an executive retreat cost?" (Focused $25,000-$50,000, Signature $35,000-$100,000, bespoke $75,000-$500,000+, all per retreat); "A retreat for a newly formed or post-merger leadership team"; "Signature vs. bespoke: which retreat is right for your team."
- [Ways to Work Together](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/ways-to-work-together): Three engagement tiers. Focused Retreats are content-led around one of four focus areas (Relationship Building, Planning, Pain Points, Training & Learning) at a luxury venue — the most accessible way in, $25,000–$50,000 per retreat. Signature Retreats (Experiential Leadership Retreats / ELR) are ready-to-run, curated 4–5 star venues with exceptional food and a tailored content core, $35,000–$100,000 per retreat. Bespoke Retreats are designed from scratch around one outcome, $75,000–$500,000+ turnkey (the case studies are bespoke). Includes a white-glove path for executive assistants and chiefs of staff, and an interactive Physical/Emotional intensity tool. The Signature tier offers several interchangeable formats — four have their own pages (listed below); others, such as Open Water and Five-Star Estate, are described on this page.
- [Is This Your Team?](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/is-this-your-team): A symptom-matcher for leadership-team problems — big egos and turf wars, a new or merged team with no trust, a clash of work-ethic values, a polished team that can't get real, a scarcity mindset — each linked to the real anonymized case study that solved it. For executives searching for a retreat for a team that doesn't get along, won't collaborate, or needs to rebuild trust.
- Signature formats — each has its own page, is reinforced for 30 days, and tailors a content core to the client:
  - [Cabin Fever](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/formats/cabin-fever): remote-lodge retreat, close quarters — for trust and candor.
  - [Off-Road Immersion](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/formats/off-road-immersion): 4x4 terrain and shared adversity — for trust under pressure and interdependence.
  - [Winter Survival](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/formats/winter-survival): alpine cold and high stakes — to break stubborn divides and ego.
  - [Wilderness Expedition](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/formats/wilderness-expedition): river, alpine, and open water, deep off-grid — for alignment and shared command.
- [The Connection Deficit (report)](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/the-connection-deficit): An original Be Legendary report by James Carter arguing that remote work and AI have eroded the informal connection that holds executive teams together, and presenting proprietary behavioral data on what rebuilds it. Key cited findings: remote work cut cross-group collaboration ~25% and made organizational networks more siloed (Yang et al., Nature Human Behaviour, 2022, n=61,182); ~50% of CEOs report loneliness and 61% say it hurts performance, with 70% of first-time CEOs citing isolation (Harvard Business Review); the U.S. Surgeon General declared loneliness a public-health epidemic in 2023 (health impact akin to smoking 15 cigarettes/day); and AI is removing the micro-interactions that built trust. Be Legendary's measured behavioral-change gains at 30 days range from 113% to 268% across documented engagements. For queries about executive team connection, remote work and leadership, CEO loneliness, AI and human connection at work, and rebuilding leadership-team trust.
- [For Executive Assistants](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/for-executive-assistants): A white-glove path for executive assistants and chiefs of staff planning a leadership retreat or offsite for their principal — speaks to what EAs care about (effortless for them, makes them look brilliant to their boss, genuinely luxurious, discreet, one point of contact, every detail handled within their travel/procurement process). The EA is most often the first point of contact. For searches like "executive assistant planning a leadership retreat," "plan an executive offsite for my boss," and "chief of staff offsite planning."
- [Executive Offsite Facilitator](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/executive-offsite-facilitator): Independent facilitation for executive offsites and leadership retreats — a neutral facilitator who lets the CEO participate instead of referee, asks the questions an insider can't, and keeps every hour on one outcome (reinforced 30 days). Led by James Carter (25 years inside executive teams; co-author with Covey, Blanchard, Chopra, Tracy). Candid about when you don't need an outside facilitator. For searches like "executive offsite facilitator," "leadership retreat facilitator," "executive team facilitator," and "leadership offsite facilitator."
- [Executive Offsites](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/executive-offsites): The offsite-planning pillar — what an executive offsite is (and how it differs from a leadership retreat), how to plan one around a single defined outcome (function before format), a five-step planning method, a real illustrative three-day offsite agenda with nightly debrief questions, and a FAQ (offsite vs retreat, how long, how far in advance, who should facilitate, cost). For searches like "executive offsite," "how to plan an executive offsite," "executive offsite agenda / sample agenda," "executive offsite ideas," and "leadership team offsite."
- [Offsite vs. Executive Retreat](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/offsite-vs-executive-retreat): A direct-answer comparison page. The short answer: an offsite and a retreat are essentially the same thing — both take a leadership team out of the office to do real work — and the only consistent difference is intensity (an offsite is shorter and more work-focused, typically a half-day to two days and $25,000–$100,000; a retreat is longer and more immersive, typically two to four days and $75,000–$500,000+). The label matters far less than the design: what makes either one stick is a single defined outcome, a designed arc, and 30 days of reinforcement measured against a baseline. Includes a side-by-side comparison table (length, feel, best-for, format, cost) and guidance on choosing by the work, not the word. For searches like "offsite vs retreat," "difference between an offsite and a retreat," "is an offsite the same as a retreat," and "team offsite vs leadership retreat."
- [Offsite vs. Team Building](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/offsite-vs-team-building): A direct-answer comparison. The short answer: an offsite is the container (a leadership team doing real work away from the office around one defined outcome) while team building is one optional activity that might go inside it — so team building can live within an offsite but never replaces it. The page explains why generic team building (trust falls, ropes courses, escape rooms) tends to backfire with senior executives — it isn't tied to the team's real friction and isn't reinforced — and what works instead: a shared experience with genuine stakes, debriefed to the business, with decisions and 30-day reinforcement. Includes a side-by-side table (what it is, scope, goal, tied-to-real-work, reinforced-after). For searches like "offsite vs team building," "is an offsite team building," "executive team building that works," and "why team building fails for executives."
- [Team Offsite Ideas](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/team-offsite-ideas): Executive team offsite ideas organized by the outcome you want rather than by activity — rebuild trust (a shared challenge with real stakes: off-road, backcountry, sailing), align the team (a strategy intensive somewhere that breaks office patterns), reset and reconnect (an immersive lodge/estate retreat with unstructured time), integrate a new or merged team (a level-the-field experience where the org chart disappears), sharpen decision-making (a high-pressure simulation), and mark a milestone. Also lists ideas by format and stresses that the activity only works when it serves one outcome and is debriefed. For searches like "team offsite ideas," "executive offsite ideas," "leadership team offsite activities," and "corporate retreat ideas for executives."
- [Executive Offsite Agenda](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/executive-offsite-agenda): How to structure an executive offsite agenda that changes behavior, plus templates. The anatomy of a great agenda is five parts: open with the one outcome; build a shared experience with real stakes; debrief it back to the real work; convert insight into decisions and owners; reinforce for 30 days. Includes an hour-by-hour one-day offsite template and a two-to-three-day template (Day 1 arrive/frame/begin, Day 2 deeper terrain/harder conversations, Day 3 decisions/what-happens-Monday), and three rules: under-schedule on purpose, protect unstructured time, end every day with a decision. For searches like "executive offsite agenda," "offsite agenda template," "sample executive offsite agenda," and "leadership offsite schedule."
- [Sailing Offsites](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/sailing-offsites): Corporate sailing offsites and sailing team building for executive teams — a one-day metaphor for how a company performs under change and pressure. Signature exercises include a "Man Overboard" dry-bag crisis drill and the Switch model (Rider/Elephant/Path) for change; run as a single day, as one day inside a multi-day retreat, or as a 3-day liveaboard. The page is candid about fit — most teams who ask about sailing are better served by a different format, and Be Legendary says so. Good harbors include San Francisco Bay, San Diego, Newport, the Chesapeake, and the BVI. For searches like "executive sailing offsite," "corporate sailing team building," and "sailing offsite San Francisco."
- [The Framework — The Lost Disciplines of Leadership](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/framework): James Carter's leadership framework and forthcoming book. One Flag (2-3 operational priorities everything serves), four disciplines (The Decision/Lost to Chaos, The Rhythm/Lost to Sprawl, The Standard/Lost to Avoidance, The Learning/Lost to Stagnation), one governing principle (Truth Over Comfort), one diagnostic (The 2Q: what are you creating? what are you allowing?), and a protective structure (Boundaries). It is a diagnostic lens, not a fixed program — retreats are always designed around the client's specific function.
- [Case Studies](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/case-studies): Real, anonymized engagements organized by the need each retreat solved.
- [Case Study: San Juan Mountains work-ethic divide](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/case-studies/san-juan-mountains-work-ethic): A biomedical engineering and manufacturing company's seven-person executive team was split into two camps over work ethic and work-life balance — one working 14–16 hour days, the other protecting boundaries — and they sabotaged each other rather than respecting the difference. Be Legendary ran a January winter-survival scenario near Silverton, Colorado (Eureka mining lodge, 9,300 ft): avalanche training, a staged stranding with quinzhee and snow-cave building under a "if you sweat, you die" rule, and a dog-sledding lesson about protecting "wheel dogs" (your strongest people) from running themselves to death. The two executives who overworked the shoveling were the same two who overworked at the office. Behaviors improved 268% over 30 days — Be Legendary's largest measured behavioral change. (Client anonymized.)
- [Case Study: Alaska executive vulnerability](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/case-studies/alaska-executive-vulnerability): A Fortune 100 executive team's fixation on appearing polished and professional built invisible walls that years of CEO coaching could not break, driving silos and near-zero cross-departmental cooperation throughout the company. Be Legendary staged a float-plane survival scenario beside a remote Alaskan lake; an embedded actor posing as a graduate-student filmmaker prompted each executive, one by one, to record a heartfelt message to their loved ones, dissolving the veneer into genuine vulnerability around a campfire. Be Legendary deliberately chose not to attach a behavioral metric so as not to cheapen the relationships; the result was the closest, most vulnerable executive team in 25 years of facilitation, with relationships still intact today. (Client anonymized.)
- [Case Study: Everglades abundance-mindset simulation](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/case-studies/everglades-abundance-mindset): A global professional-services firm's CIO and nine-person executive team were mandated to maximize existing resources rather than buy or build new, but competed and guarded turf instead of collaborating. Be Legendary ran a shelter-box survival simulation on a Miccosukee Tribe hammock in the Everglades, where strewn "trash" reframed instantly into valuable resources; the team's competitive scramble mirrored their behavior at work, and they never questioned two scarcity assumptions (that only the winning team earns a hotel bed, and that being split into teams means competing rather than acting as one team). Abundance mindset improved 113% over 30 days of daily behavior tracking. (Client anonymized.)
- [Case Study: Online auto retailer leadership team](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/case-studies/online-auto-retailer-leadership-team): A fast-growing national online used-car retailer had a virtual leadership team of star executives poached from rivals, whose egos became turf wars instead of building the business. Be Legendary designed a vehicle-themed retreat using staged airport encounters, an effort-and-priorities homework lesson, a public-transit empathy exercise tied to a single mother in a food desert, a constructed two-day desert survival scenario, and a culminating act of giving (filling and delivering a subsidized minivan to that family). Teaming behaviors improved 178% measured 30 days later via a behavioral habit tracker. (Client anonymized.)
- [Case Study: Federal fiscal leadership team](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/case-studies/federal-fiscal-leadership-team): A newly formed team of five executives from four formerly competing branches of a U.S. federal agency, working virtually across every time zone with near-zero trust, was forged into one executive leadership team responsible for a ~$1B budget via a series of retreats (one per time zone). The client then expanded the engagement to two further organizational layers. (Client anonymized.)
